correctness.rationale: The scalar recurrence is an exact specialization of the source algorithm. The per-step objective ratio is a square, making the universal threshold equivalent to the classical interval for the current effective scaled step. Necessity follows from an exact first-step calculation. The arbitrary finite ascent claim follows by a finite-horizon continuity induction showing gamma_k=varsigma+O(x_0^2) and x_j/x_0 tending to the stated power.

value.rationale: The sharp dimensionless threshold separates two qualitatively different transient regimes on a condition-number-one problem. Above it, the minimizer with the startup accumulator is a genuine local repeller and any prescribed finite number of objective increases can be forced by moving the start closer to the minimizer. This goes beyond a single cheap overshoot example and clarifies why hyperparameter-robust convergence does not imply monotone or benign transients.
